To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a (6)Li-based thermal neutron detector was developed for the NESCOFI spectrometry project.

(1) the detector is able to detect thermal neutrons with a time resolution better than 10 ns; (2) the energy resolution is 0.6 eV (3) the efficiency is 2.4% (4) the detector is stable over time (5) the device is sensitive also to gamma rays (6) the device is able to detect fast neutrons (7) the device has a small size (8) the device has low weight.
the thermal neutron pulse detector is suitable to be used in the NESCOFI assembly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a thermal neutron detector based on a semiconductor device coupled with a suitable radiator to improve the thermal neutron sensitivity.
the development of a compact neutron detector with a high sensitivity to thermal neutrons.
the design, construction and testing of a thermal neutron detector based on (7)LiF: Mg, Ti scintillator coupled to a photomultiplier tube (PMT).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the detector has a good thermal neutron detection efficiency, but the response is affected by the presence of a large number of background events, which are due to the presence of the gamma-ray source used for calibration and to the intrinsic background of the detector.
the detector under investigation is a good compromise between the required sensitivity and the compactness.
the device is suitable for use as a thermal neutron pulse sensor in a moderator-based neutron spectrometer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the (6)Li detector has a very high efficiency for thermal neutrons and a good time resolution (1-2 ns).
a thermal neutron detector with a 1 mm thick (6)LiF:ZnS(Ag) scintillator and a Si photodiode has been characterised.

the (6)Li-based detector is a promising solution for the realization of compact thermal neutron detectors, with a good sensitivity and a low background, which could be used for the development of a new moderator-based neutron spectrometer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pulse shape of a detector can be used as a tool to characterise the detector itself and its response to the neutron flux.
the (6)Li-based thermal neutron sensor can be used as a fast and compact neutron detector for the measurement of the neutron spectrum in the energy range between 10 eV and 10 keV.
this sensor can be used as a thermal neutron detector in a moderator-based neutron spectrometer.
